claims.explanation: Crizotinib selectively kills cancer cell lines that depend on the kinase activity of its targets ALK, MET, or ROS1, most commonly through genomic rearrangements or amplification of these genes. In the screened lines, sensitivity is best explained by MET amplification/mutation (e.g., HGC27, HT115) and possibly ALK or ROS1 fusions, while lines without such alterations are largely resistant. The drug's known clinical activity against ALK- and ROS1-rearranged tumors supports this target-driven selectivity.
